newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-HALL TO HEAD WEST INDIES SELECTION COMMITTEE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HALL TO HEAD WEST INDIES SELECTION COMMITTEE.

text.p: Former test fast bowler and team manager Wes Hall has been voted chairman of West Indies selection panel, the West Indies Cricket Board of Control (WICBC) said.
A spokesman said on Saturday that Hall was elected at the WICBC general meeting in Antigua. He replaces fellow Barbadian David Holford, who did not seek re-election.
Holford has been appointed manager of the Barbados team for the 1997 first-class season which includes a two-round Red Stripe Cup between the six regional teams for the first time.
Former test opener Joey Carew of Trinidad and Tobago and wicketkeeper Michael Findlay of St Vincent were also elected to the selection committee.
Carew is a past chairman of the selection panel while Findlay will be serving for the first time.
The panel is completed by West Indies' coach Malcolm Marshall and the captain Courtney Walsh.
Carew and Findlay replace Guyanese Joe Solomon and Jamaican Easton McMorris.

In a separate move, WICBC chief executive Steve Camacho said former captain Viv Richards had agreed to join the management team of Marshall and Clive Loyd with a brief to coach throughout the Caribbean islands.
"It is wonderful. Our young players can only benefit from listening to the advice from one of the world's greatest players," Camacho said.
The appointment signals the end of a log-running rift between Richards and the board.
